summary: This program asks two yes/no questions and recommends one of four desserts, using an if statement placed inside another if statement to combine the two answers.

lines.text: input always hands back text, so .strip() removes any stray spaces or the newline and .lower() turns "Y" into "y" 	ing only has to be compared against one form.
This is the outer decision, and it splits the program into the hot-day world and the cool-day world before the chocolate question is even considered.
The extra level of indentation is what makes this a nested decision: it is only reached when the outer condition was true, so it decides between the two hot-day desserts.
This else lines up with the outer if, not the inner one, so it opens the cool-day branch that holds its own complete if/else pair.
Every one of the four paths assigns dessert, so by the time this line runs the name is guaranteed to exist; leaving one branch out would crash here.
